summary: Food scientists design and package space food so it stays safe, tasty, and crumb-free when astronauts eat it in a floating spacecraft.
introduce: Write the key term “dehydrated” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “Space Food: Eating Without Gravity” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: having had almost all the water removed, often to make food last longer
a small, flexible bag used to hold and protect something
to mix completely into a liquid until it disappears as a solid

challengeTerms.def: describing food that has been cooked and sealed using heat so it stays safe without refrigeration
likely to spoil or decay quickly unless eaten or stored carefully
a substance in food that the body needs to stay healthy and grow

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that eating food in space is harder than eating it on Earth? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Choose one method used to prepare or package space food.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review dehydrated, pouch, and dissolve, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses thermostabilized, perishable, and nutrient to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
